question: What is the primary definition of a poison in clinical practice?

options.A: Any substance that disrupts body function or causes cellular damage
options.B: A strictly manufactured chemical compound used in industrial settings
options.C: A medicinal drug taken strictly above the prescribed dosage limit
options.D: An organic substance that only affects the respiratory system

explanation: A poison is broadly defined as any agent that causes structural damage or functional disturbance when introduced to the body. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why do community health nurses play a vital role in managing poisoning cases?

options.A: They perform advanced surgical interventions for all toxicological emergencies
options.B: They provide frontline recognition, stabilization, and public safety education
options.C: They regulate the importation of dangerous chemical substances
options.D: They are solely responsible for manufacturing antidotes in laboratories

explanation: Primary healthcare nurses are usually the first professional contact, making their rapid assessment and preventive guidance essential for survival. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h1)

question: Which household item is a frequent cause of accidental poisoning among toddlers in Nigeria?

options.B: Kerosene stored in soft drink bottles

explanation: Storing hazardous liquids like kerosene in familiar beverage containers frequently misleads children into accidental ingestion. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h2)

question: A farmer presents with excessive salivation, lacrimation, and muscle twitching after spraying his crops. Which category of poison is most likely responsible?
explanation: Organophosphates inhibit acetylcholinesterase, leading to cholinergic excess symptoms such as salivation, lacrimation, urination, and muscle fasciculations. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the most frequent route of toxic exposure in domestic settings?
explanation: Swallowing toxic substances, particularly household chemicals or medications, accounts for the highest percentage of domestic poisoning cases. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h3)

question: How do inhaled toxic gases rapidly enter the systemic circulation?

options.A: By being filtered first through the hepatic portal system
options.B: Across the thin alveolar-capillary membrane in the lungs
options.C: Through direct absorption via the outer epidermal skin layer
options.D: Via active transport across the gastric mucosal lining

explanation: The massive surface area and rich blood supply of the alveoli allow inhaled gases to pass directly into the bloodstream very quickly. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h3)

question: Which clinical sign is characteristic of an opioid overdose toxidrome?
explanation: Opioid toxicity classically presents with central nervous system depression, pinpoint pupils (miosis), and dangerously slow breathing. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why is identifying a specific toxidrome clinically useful for the nursing team?

options.A: It confirms the exact brand name of the chemical ingested
options.B: It replaces the need for taking a history from the relatives
options.C: It guides immediate empirical nursing care before definitive lab results arrive
options.D: It eliminates the need to monitor patient vital signs every hour

explanation: Toxidromes group symptoms together so clinicians can recognize the general class of poison and start appropriate supportive care quickly. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h4)

question: What is the recommended immediate action for a patient with chemical exposure on the skin?

options.A: Remove contaminated clothing and flush the skin with copious water
options.B: Apply concentrated palm oil over the affected skin surface
options.C: Apply a tight bandage to prevent systemic spread of the toxin
options.D: Scrub the chemical off firmly using a dry surgical brush

explanation: Washing the skin with plenty of water dilutes and removes the chemical agent, stopping continuous dermal absorption. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why is inducing vomiting discouraged in patients who swallowed corrosive substances?

options.A: It immediately triggers irreversible cardiac arrest in all patients
options.B: It neutralizes the antidote before it can be administered
options.C: It causes secondary chemical burns to the esophagus and increases aspiration risks
options.D: It forces the toxin to move faster into the large intestine

explanation: Brings corrosive substances back up re-exposes the delicate esophageal tissue to burning and raises the danger of fluid entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which strategy is most effective for preventing childhood poisoning in rural communities?

options.A: Educating caregivers on keeping chemicals in original, labeled containers out of reach
options.B: Storing agricultural pesticides inside domestic food pantries
options.C: Teaching children how to perform gastric lavage on each other
options.D: Banning the importation of all household cleaning agents

explanation: Public health education focusing on safe storage prevents accidental ingestion by keeping toxic agents away from curious children. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h6)

question: A community health nurse notices local shopkeepers selling acid in unlabelled soft drink bottles. What is the appropriate intervention?

options.A: Confiscate the items and fine the customers buying them
options.B: Refer all affected buyers directly to the surgical ward
options.C: Ignore the practice as it is common economic activity
options.D: Educate the shopkeepers on the dangers and promote proper labeling

explanation: Targeting the source of improper storage through direct education prevents accidental poisonings in the wider community. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h6)

question: Where should hazardous household chemicals ideally be stored at home?

options.A: Uncovered on the floor of the bedroom
options.B: Inside empty beverage bottles on the dining table
options.C: Under the kitchen sink for easy daily access
options.D: In a locked cupboard high out of the reach of children

explanation: Securing chemicals in high, locked storage areas physically prevents young children from accessing and ingesting them. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h7)

question: Why is reusing empty agrochemical containers for domestic water storage dangerous?

options.A: Toxic chemical residues can leach into the water and cause poisoning
options.B: Plastic containers degrade quickly when exposed to sunlight
options.C: It increases the growth of harmless algae inside the container
options.D: The water will change its natural color immediately

explanation: Chemical residues cling to plastic materials and cannot be easily washed out, contaminating any water stored inside later. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h7)
